elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The inserted Work Product clause grants Client only a licence ("TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense all results of the Support Services"); no operative sentence vests ownership of the results/work product in Client.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; the redline uses a licence construct only.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 2(d) retained unchanged: "Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The Work Product grant is by TrueLink and covers "all results of the Support Services and any other work product prepared for Client" (which carries any TrueLink IP embedded in them) and is expressly "perpetual".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The redline adds no Customer Data ownership sentence; the rationale points to a Section 13 "Client Content" ownership sentence, but it is not rendered here and it is not established that it reaches Credit Data. To meet this element the drafter must add an express sentence that Client retains all right, title and interest in Credit Data and other Client data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 8(d) as redlined: "license to use, upload, display, copy and store Credit Data solely to provide the Hosting Services and Support Services to Client" — the distribute/disseminate/license/resell/exploit rights that constituted independent exploitation are deleted.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language appears in the cited or rendered provisions; the redline creates none.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 2(d) untouched: TrueLink "retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface" — Vendor platform/tool ownership preserved, which is permitted.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted Work Product clause: "perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense all results of the Support Services and any other work product prepared for Client under this Agreement".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same clause states "irrevocable" with no revocation or termination-linked cut-off.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Same clause states "royalty-free"; no further fee is imposed.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense all results of the Support Services and any other work product ... for Client's business purposes".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Same clause expressly includes "sublicense ... for Client's business purposes"; no consent condition attached.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Redlined Section 8(d) confines TrueLink's Credit Data licence to "use, upload, display, copy and store ... solely to provide the Hosting Services and Support Services to Client", removing the distribute/resell/exploit rights.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the inserted Work Product clause supplies all six deliverables-licence attributes (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, use/modify, sublicense, for Client's business purposes) over "all results of the Support Services and any other work product prepared for Client", Section 2(d) already leaves TrueLink owning the Interface, and Section 8(d) is narrowed to processing Credit Data solely to provide the Hosting and Support Services.

Preferred level fails on two operative points the drafter would have to fix: (a) no sentence vesting ownership of the deliverables/work product in Client and no assignment by TrueLink, and (b) no express statement that Client retains all right, title and interest in Credit Data / Client data (reliance on a Section 13 Client Content sentence is unverified and may not reach Credit Data).

Minimal: the only deletions are the exploitation verbs ("distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit") that directly defeat the Customer Data element, the favourable Non-Competition Agreement limitation is retained verbatim, and the added Work Product sentence is a concise insertion filling a genuinely absent clause with no survival tail, expense, indemnity or procedural extras.

Preserves intent: Section 4 Support Services and Section 2(d) are untouched, the retained "subject to ... the Non-Competition Agreement" qualifier still operates, and no cross-reference is left dangling; the added grant uses the Agreement's own Hosting Services / Support Services concepts rather than a new undefined term.
